technical_and_design_decisions: Implement dynamic module contributions through the existing Spring Cloud Data Flow module registry service rather than retaining bootstrap-time hard-coded registration.
Persist module metadata in the existing registry persistence mechanism and make successful contributions immediately queryable by stream and task definition creation flows.
Expose module contribution through authenticated REST endpoints and corresponding shell commands, reusing existing command and API conventions.
Store uploaded module artifacts using the platform's existing artifact storage/configuration where available; retain coordinates and metadata in the module registry.
Validate module type, name, version, URI or artifact coordinates, and duplicate-version behavior at the service boundary.
Preserve backward compatibility for existing preconfigured modules and existing stream/task definition APIs.
Migrate the six Spring XD modules as independently buildable Spring Cloud Stream modules, adapting configuration, metadata, tests, and packaging to the target repository conventions.
Use the existing supported Java and Spring versions of the target repositories and avoid introducing a new messaging or persistence technology.
Add automated unit and integration coverage for registry operations, REST and shell flows, and each migrated module's primary behavior.
assumptions: The existing Spring Cloud Data Flow codebase, module registry persistence, REST infrastructure, shell framework, and module build templates are available and functional.
Authentication, authorization, artifact storage, and database provisioning are already present; this increment only integrates with them and does not introduce a new identity or storage subsystem.
The required REST and shell API conventions can be extended without a major versioning redesign.

Acceptance criteria for upload, replacement, deletion, duplicate versions, and validation are not specified; the implementation will reject invalid or conflicting contributions with clear errors and will not silently overwrite an existing module version.

Module artifacts may be supplied by supported URI or Maven-style coordinates; arbitrary local filesystem uploads and distributed artifact replication are out of scope unless already supported by the platform.
The six modules have usable Spring XD source code and tests that can be adapted, with no substantial reimplementation of their business behavior required.
The references to the s-c-s and s-c-s-m repositories are treated as the target Spring Cloud Stream module repositories, with repository naming differences resolved during setup.

Work is estimated for one developer and includes coding, review/self-review, automated testing, documentation, and build verification, but excludes elapsed waiting time for external approvals or infrastructure provisioning.
A workday represents eight hours of productive effort.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing module registry bootstrap, persistence model, REST controllers, shell commands, module packaging conventions, and Spring XD source modules; define API behavior, metadata mapping, validation rules, and migration boundaries.

activities.activity_name: Dynamic module registry domain and persistence changes
activities.activity_description: Replace or extend bootstrap-only registration with service-layer registration, persistence of module metadata, lookup integration, duplicate/version handling, and compatibility behavior for existing preconfigured modules.

Implement authenticated REST operations for contributing module metadata and artifact references, including request mapping, validation, error responses, persistence, and immediate registry visibility.
Add shell commands for module contribution and registry inspection, including command options, input validation, REST client integration, human-readable errors, and help text.

activities.activity_name: Upload validation, security, and operational behavior
activities.activity_description: Integrate authorization checks, artifact URI or coordinate validation, module type validation, duplicate handling, transaction boundaries, logging, and safe failure behavior for invalid contributions.

Create unit and integration tests covering persistence, registration and lookup, REST operations, shell commands, validation failures, duplicate versions, authorization behavior, and use of newly contributed modules in definitions.
Move the JMS source module into the target repository, adapt dependencies and configuration metadata, update packaging and documentation, and port or repair module tests.
Move the mail source module into the target repository, adapt Spring Cloud Stream integration and configuration metadata, update packaging and documentation, and port or repair tests.
Move the Mongo source module into the target repository, adapt Mongo dependencies, configuration, metadata, packaging, documentation, and module tests.
Move the MQTT source module into the target repository, adapt MQTT client and binder integration, configuration metadata, packaging, documentation, and tests.
Move the reactor-ip source module, adapt reactive networking dependencies and configuration, update module metadata and packaging, and port or repair tests.
Move the stdout source module, adapt the target repository conventions and configuration metadata, update packaging and documentation, and port or repair tests.

Build all migrated modules against the supported Java/Spring versions, verify artifact publication and registry contribution, exercise representative stream definitions, and resolve cross-module or dependency conflicts.
Document REST and shell contribution workflows, metadata requirements, validation and versioning behavior, migrated module properties, and representative streaming pipeline examples.

activities.activity_name: Build, CI, release, and final quality verification
activities.activity_description: Update build descriptors and CI jobs, verify licensing and repository layout, run the complete test suite and static checks, perform self-review, and prepare release notes or migration notes.
